app.name: Sanguine
taglines: The River of Blood never empties; it only crests.
By blood bound, by brass crowned.
Offerings of bone, rivers of red.
The earth drinks deep, yet the Blood God thirsts.
An ocean of red for the Lord of Rage.

s1.title: Track and understand your cycle
s1.body: Sanguine estimates when your next period and your ovulation are likely, using what you log. Estimates are ranges, not promises. Sanguine is not a contraceptive and is not a medical device.

how.title: How Sanguine estimates
how.rowDesc: How the ranges are worked out, what the confidence words mean and what changes them.
how.rangeTitle: Where the period range comes from
how.rangeBody: Sanguine looks at the lengths of your last 12 cycles. Before you have logged a few, it starts from published averages for your age group (Bull et al. 2019) and moves towards your own pattern as cycles are added. In most life states, recent cycles and older ones count the same. A cycle that looks like a missed log, or that falls in a life change you set (such as pregnancy, or the months after stopping a hormonal method), is left out or counted less. The result is the range of days that has an 80% likelihood of holding your next period start; the calendar also shows the wider 95% range.
how.confidenceHigh: Confident: at least six cycles and a period range no wider than about a week.
how.confidenceMedium: Fair estimate: at least two cycles and a period range of up to about 11 days.
how.confidenceLow: Rough estimate: fewer than two cycles, or cycles that vary so much the range is wider than about 11 days. The range is wide on purpose.
how.confidenceNone: No estimate: not enough data yet, or a life change you set pauses the estimates.
how.narrowBody: Logging every period start, including the first day, matters most. Morning temperature, ovulation tests, cervical mucus and cervical position can date ovulation in a cycle after it happens, which sharpens the next period estimate and the fertile window estimate.
how.narrowBodyTeen: Logging every period start, including the first day, matters most. The more cycles you log, the narrower the range becomes.
how.symptomsTitle: What does not change the estimates
how.symptomsBody: Symptoms, mood and notes never change an estimate. They show up in Insights so you can see your own patterns, but there is no published evidence that they predict when a period starts.
how.accuracyTitle: How well it has done for you
how.accuracyBody: When a cycle ends, Sanguine checks whether the range it gave at the start of that cycle held the real start date. Insights, Your accuracy, shows the count.

calendar.rowDesc: Send your predicted period range as a calendar file.
calendar.intro: This makes a calendar file with your predicted period as a range of days. You send it with the share sheet, for example to a partner, who adds it to their calendar. Nothing is sent unless you send it.

calendar.eventTitleHelp: What the other calendar shows. A single letter keeps it private.
calendar.includeFertileDesc: Added as a range of days, never a single day. It is an estimate only.
calendar.resend: To update the dates later, send a new file. Calendars that recognise the event replace it; in others, delete the earlier event first.
calendar.failed: The calendar file could not be shared.

privacy.title: Privacy and data
privacy.intro: Your data is stored only on this phone, in an encrypted database. Sanguine has no account and no server.
privacy.exportDesc: A zip with JSON and CSV files.
privacy.importDesc: Sanguine export, Natural Cycles or drip export, or a CSV of period start dates.
privacy.backupDesc: Saves an encrypted file you can keep anywhere.
privacy.appLockDesc: Use Face ID, fingerprint or your passcode to open Sanguine.
privacy.discreetIconDesc: Shows a leaf icon on your home screen. Reminders and widgets say Notes.
privacy.discreetIconDescAndroid: Shows the app as Notes, with a leaf icon, on your home screen. The app closes when this changes; open it again from the home screen.
privacy.screenProtection: Hide the app in screenshots and recent apps
privacy.screenProtectionDesc: On: screenshots and the recent-apps picture are blocked. The recovery code screen always blocks them.
privacy.consentGiven: Given on {date}. To withdraw it, delete your data.
privacy.consentNone: No consent is recorded on this phone.
privacy.deleteConfirmBody: This removes every log, setting and backup key from this phone. It cannot be undone. Backups you saved in iCloud Drive, Google Drive or Files, and entries written to Apple Health or Health Connect, stay where they are until you delete them there.
privacy.exportFailed: The export could not be made.
privacy.importNotesDropped: {n} notes were skipped because the file has no notes column.
privacy.importFailed: That file could not be read.

cloud.linkHelp: This phone then uses the same code, and both phones merge their entries through the copy.
cloud.title: Cloud copy
cloud.switchDesc: Uploads an encrypted copy after changes, on Wi-Fi, at most once an hour. Turning this on keeps a key made from your passphrase in this phone's secure storage. On more than one phone, each phone merges the others' entries from the copy first.
cloud.needPass: Type your backup passphrase above first.
cloud.waitingWifi: Saved. The first upload happens when this phone is on Wi-Fi.
cloud.failed: Could not reach {service}. Sanguine will try again.
cloud.unavailable: {service} is not available on this phone.
cloud.none: There is no backup in {service} yet.
cloud.off: Cloud copy is off. The key was removed from this phone; the file in {service} stays until you delete it there.

privacy.backupNote: Keep the passphrase and recovery code somewhere private. Without them the backup cannot be opened, by design.
